episodes.170844: An isolated instance of flash flooding occurred due to heavy rainfall from a thunderstorm in Prince Georges County.
episodes.170894: A thunderstorm produced localized, minor wind damage near Riverdale just northeast of DC.
episodes.170902: A couple thunderstorms produced gusty winds over the middle Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.170934: Despite the upper-level high pressure system building over the Four Corners, a backdoor cold front moved southward through eastern and central New Mexico on August 8, 2022. This influx of moisture helped to support a robust round of thunderstorms throughout the afternoon and evening hours. A magnet for heavy thunderstorms, the Calf Canyon burn scar was impacted again with significant flash flooding and debris flow reported in the Rociada, Holman, and Chacon areas.
episodes.170935: Torrential rainfall, up to 2.5 inches in 20 minutes, produced flash flooding in and around the Denver area.  The heavy rainfall flooded the underpass at 38th and Blake, as well as Interstate 70, from Brighton Blvd to York St.  Denver firefighters rescued 19 people from those locations alone.  Floodwaters knocked down a retaining wall in Thornton at 8600 Washington St.  Flooding and tree damage also occurred at the Denver Zoo. Six to 12 inches of standing water was observed at 47th and Lincoln.  Flooding also observed at 16th and Franklin St.  Intense winds from a wet microburst, downed a tree in Denver which fell onto vehicle parked nearby along 13th St. in Capitol Hill.
episodes.171306: With a stationary boundary well to our northwest, and high pressure centered to our southeast, KY found itself in a weak return flow pattern. Winds were relatively light, with strong subsidence aloft thanks to an upper level ridge in place. Severe weather was not expected during the day, with most of the eastern conus in just a general thunderstorm risk. That being said, a few showers and thunderstorms did develop. Without a strong steering flow, the shower was slow to move, and therefore ended up leading to an isolated report of flooding in Perry County.
episodes.171443: Multiple rounds of monsoonal thunderstorms occurred on August 7th through the 9th. A few severe thunderstorms produced high winds, while many others produced very heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.171653: A surface front moved little across central Lake Michigan, northern Lower Michigan, and southern Ontario from the early evening of the 7th through afternoon of the 8th. By the early evening of the 8th, the front had moved southeastward as a cold front to northwest Ohio, central Lake Erie, and the northwest Lake Ontario shore as a low developed northeastward along the surface front in southern Ontario. Ahead of the front, multiple rounds of thunderstorms with gale-force to storm-force peak wind gusts impacted western and central Lake Erie as they encountered primarily weak to moderate MUCAPE and effective bulk shear, respectively, and moderate to strong DCAPE within the warm sector.
episodes.171854: Heavy rain caused flash flooding across parts of northwest Illinois during the morning of August 8th when rainfall of 3 to 5 inches with locally higher amounts fell.  Previous rainfall the day before brought two day rainfall totals to 6 to 9 inches across many areas across northwest Illinois.  A church was struck by lightning in Rockford during the morning of August 8th causing significant damage.  Rockford Airport measured a two day rain total of 6.15 inches for August 7th and 8th with 3.23 inches on August 8th which set a new rain record for the day.
episodes.171855: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the morning of August 8th.
episodes.171871: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around west central Florida.
episodes.171872: Afternoon thunderstorms produce a brief tornado near Charlotte Park in Charlotte County, damaging lightning strikes in Pinellas and Lee counties, severe hail near Kenneth City in Pinellas County and localized street flooding in St. Petersburg in Pinellas County.
episodes.172091: A mid-level shear axis moved westward into Arkansas. Diurnal showers and thunderstorms developed along the shear axis and produced heavy rainfall and damaging wind.
episodes.172171: A Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough (TUTT) retrograded over the FL peninsula during the day with cooler than normal mid level temperatures (-9 degC at 500 mb). This increased mid level instability combined with diurnal instability and prevailing SE steering flow focused the afternoon sea breeze mergers near I-75 where strong to severe storms developed.
episodes.172781: Numerous heavy rains and severe thunderstorms developed all across the region during the afternoon and evening of August 7th. Numerous flash floods, mud and debris slides, and damaging winds and hail were all reported as storms moved from the central mountains onto the eastern CO plains.
episodes.172837: Storms moved across southwest Wisconsin during the early morning hours of August 8th. These storms produced heavy rainfall with radar estimates of 2 to 2.5 inches. Runoff from this heavy rain caused some rock slides to occur near Potosi (Grant County). A few culverts became clogged with debris, sending water over State Highway 133.
episodes.172923: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173005: The set up was a broad longwave trough in place over much of the Bering Sea through southern Alaska. Embedded in this broad longwave trough was an upper level low meandering over the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta. Multiple upper level shortwaves rotated around this upper level low along with a jet stream aimed right up Cook Inlet into Southcentral. The southwesterly flow at 700 millibars was also very moist with all this moisture being advected northeastward into the Cook Inlet region and Mat-SU Valleys. As a result, heavy rain occurred throughout the region resulting in flooding for some areas.
episodes.173141: Summertime heating during the day, combined with high moisture levels, prompted the development of showers and storms. One of these storms increased to severe levels and produced damaging winds.
episodes.173255: After several days of drier weather, moisture surged back across northern Arizona with more flash flooding.
episodes.173256: Abundant moisture (PWATs 1.75-2.00 inches) and instability (MLCAPE 1000+ J/KG) combined with an approaching upper-level trough to result in an environment favorable for strong convective activity. Thunderstorms first developed across the Mogollon Rim and White Mountains during the early to mid afternoon hours and then slowly drifted southwestward towards south-central Arizona. Activity affected portions of Gila County, where significant water flow was observed along the Russell Gulch area. Additional activity moved from the higher terrain down into western portions of the Phoenix metro during the early evening hours, where damaging winds and blowing dust were observed.
episodes.173285: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the area with isolated reports of damaging downburst winds during the afternoon and evening of the 8th.
episodes.173298: An upper-level trough combined with strong instability (SB CAPE of 2000+ J/KG) and high moisture content (PWAT of 1.7+ inches) to result in the development of strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Riverside and Imperial Counties during the afternoon and early evening hours. A complex of thunderstorms originating from southwest Arizona moved westward through Riverside while intensifying in the process. Another complex of storms then developed near the international border and affected Imperial County.
episodes.173338: Afternoon thunderstorms created lightning that caused damage and an injury in western Florida.
episodes.173339: Afternoon thunderstorms created lightning that caused damage in southwest Alabama.
episodes.173367: As August began, drought conditions were widespread in Arkansas, with dryness the most noticeable in northern and western sections of the state. Above normal temperatures were also common. On the 8th, a cold front approached from the north, and brought chances of rain and promised temporary relief from the heat.||Ahead of the front, thermometers showed readings in the 90s. During peak heating, thunderstorms popped up quickly in the northern half of the state. Some of the storms cranked out damaging winds. Trees were downed at Gravel Ridge and Macon (both in Pulaski County), with one tree on a fence. More trees were toppled in west Little Rock (Pulaski County). The trees fell on power lines and a home, and power outages lasted into the overnight hours for some residents. Tree damage was also noted in Hot Springs (Garland County), and several utility poles were snapped. This was the most severe weather reported during the month.||Locations with an inch or more of rainfall were few and far between. Bogg Springs (Polk County) received 2.02 inches of rain, 1.16 inches at Mena (Polk County), 1.07 inches at Hot Springs (Garland County), and 1.00 inch at Batesville (Independence County).
episodes.173406: A southward shift in the Westerlies forced a slow moving front to move southeastward into the Ozarks Region on the 8th. The front then stalled and interacted with several upper level disturbances to produce heavy rainfall and severe storms over the area through the early afternoon of the 9th. The strongest storms occurred during the afternoon and evening of the 9th, producing widespread damaging wind gusts which blew down trees and powerlines, and hail to the size of ping pong balls. The hardest hit areas were along and south of Interstate 44 from Joplin to Springfield to south of Lebanon. Rainfall accumulations of two to over four inches occurred from the Lake of the Ozarks to Stockton Lake and then southward toward Springfield, Mount Vernon and Neosho.
episodes.173408: A fairly typical summer-time air mass was in place on the 8th of August with abundant moisture throughout the atmospheric column and warm temperatures. As thunderstorms developed in the coastal waters, a couple were able to use increased low level moisture to intensify and produce short-lived waterspouts.
episodes.173419: Thunderstorms produced localized heavy rainfall causing flooding.
episodes.173458: Two rounds of showers and thunderstorms tracked from northeast Iowa into northern Illinois Sunday morning, and again early Monday morning, bringing torrential rain and occasional lightning to the region.  Rainfall amounts over 2 inches were common northeast of a line from Cedar Rapids, to De Witt, to Prophetstown IL.  The highest amounts between 5 and 11 inches fell in eastern Jo Daviess and Stephenson counties in northwest IL.  This caused numerous road closures in the county and floodwaters impacting homes in Freeport, IL.
episodes.173468: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines.
episodes.173478: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts with impacts to trees and power lines along with heavy rain which resulted in localized flooding.
episodes.173560: Sunshine over the Finger Lakes on the brought sufficient sunshine to bring ample instability to a very moist air mass that was in place. The atmosphere was not highly sheared, however. Thunderstorms first developed east of Lake Ontario with some degree of rotation involved. The second round of storms was a line of convection that rolled in from Lake Erie during the early evening. Winds aloft were around 40 knots and with a linear structure, this resulted in localized gusts in the Lake Erie marine layer as well as some trees down in the Buffalo.
episodes.173561: Sunshine over the Finger Lakes on the brought sufficient sunshine to bring ample instability to a very moist air mass that was in place. The atmosphere was not highly sheared, however. Thunderstorms first developed east of Lake Ontario with some degree of rotation involved. The second round of storms was a line of convection that rolled in from Lake Erie during the early evening. Winds aloft were around 40 knots and with a linear structure, this resulted in localized gusts in the Lake Erie marine layer as well as some trees down in the Buffalo.
episodes.173612: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the late afternoon and evening. Storms produced large hail and damaging winds in the Sierra Vista. Heavy rain caused flash flooding in St. David and far eastern Pima County.
episodes.173793: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173794: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southeast California. Several storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173865: The combination of deep tropical moisture and a weak stalled frontal boundary led to scattered showers and thunderstorms across the southern Texas Panhandle initially, with activity spreading north through the afternoon and evening.  There was moderate instability, but extremely weak wind shear present in the atmosphere and storms were disorganized, pulsy in nature.  The strongest storms occurred where outflow boundaries collided in the late afternoon and evening.  One strong boundary collision just east of Dumas, Texas led to an unusually strong and long-lived landspout that developed on the northern edge of a thunderstorm, which was generated by the boundary collision.  The landspout moved nearly due north and was on the ground for around 6 minutes and just shy of 2 miles.
episodes.173884: A strong cold front moved through the region, generating widespread showers and storms. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.174034: A backdoor cold front pushed southwest across Northern New Hampshire on the evening of August 8th.  This frontal boundary interacted with an unstable airmass and some marginal shear, which allowed a few storms to develop with an isolated report of damaging wind gusts in rural Northern New Hampshire.
episodes.177586: Scattered afternoon thunderstorms developed across portions of Mississippi on August 7th and 8th. A few of these storms were severe and produced damaging wind gusts.

The Surprise Emergency Manager said there was significant flash flooding in the Asante Community, with evidence of water over the roads. The Emergency Manager also shared there was significant mud and runoff at a water treatment plant near 29 Palms RV Park. On social media there were several reports of at least minor street flooding around the area as well. Timing of impacts estimated from radar. No reports of damage or injuries from flooding.

A 77 mph wind gust was measured at the Buckeye Municipal Airport. Triple G Dairy Farm, just to the south of the airport, experienced a lot of damage, including shattered windows from flying debris or hail, a few downed power poles, uprooted trees, metal roof partially torn off one building, and at least minor damage to nearby homes owned by dairy workers. A month after the storm, NWS Phoenix was contacted by a claims specialist looking into a hangar door that was blown off at the airport. Although unconfirmed, this storm, with the 77 mph gust, is the most probable cause of the hangar door damage. Estimated damage costs for the hangar door are applied to this event. No injuries were reported.
Two semis flipped on I-10 westbound in Buckeye, just west of SR-85, causing both lanes to be temporarily blocked. No injuries were reported.
Local broadcast showed footage of significant damage in the Buckeye area, including roofs partially torn off and a destroyed RV. No other specific details were received. No injuries were reported.

Some backyards were under nearly one foot of water and widespread basement flooding was reported.

Numerous intersections were flooded in the Rockford area.  Broadway Street and Eastmoreland Avenue was closed due to flooding and Sandy Hollow Road and Alpine Road was closed due to flooding.  Several creeks reached at least bankfull including Keith Creek near Charles Street and Hunter Avenue.

Standing water was reported at the Route 2 railroad underpass around 4:30 am CST which worsened to a depth of four feet an hour later.  A private weather station measured 5.29 inches of rain 3 miles east northeast of Bryon.
The Emergency Manager reported flooded roadways with water over the tops of fire hydrants on some of the streets on the northwest side of the city.
A small, typically dry ditch was out of its banks near Linden Road and Brookdale Road.

Standing water was reported in the Polo Fire Protection District Fire Station with knee deep water outside in the yard.  Two roads were closed due to flooding.  Basement flooding affected 35 houses.  Measured rainfall of 5.50 inches was reported in Polo with 3.50 inches falling in just 100 minutes.
A trained spotter reports a road washed out with deep water running over the road. | The road is impassable at this location.

Social media pictures and broadcast media reports indicate that flash flooding caused a home foundation to cave in with water getting into the house. The time of the event is based off of social media and radar data.

Lightning struck the St. James Catholic Church at the corner of Prairie Street and 2nd Street.  A fire started and caused significant damage to the building.  A total of 47 firefighters battled the fire.  Three of the firefighters suffered non-life threatening injuries and were taken to local hospitals.

Flooding was verified by Alaska State Troopers in Wasilla. The Regional Operations Center and the State Emergency Operations Center reported on August 8th, 2022 at approximately 22:09 hours, Alaska State Troopers (AST) began receiving multiple 911 calls reporting flooding in the area of Schrock Road and Sitze Road in Wasilla.  AST responded to the area discovering the road has been washed out and is impassible just past the Little Susitna River Bridge due to a culvert failing.  Matsu Borough along with DOT is on scene working to repair the culvert and roadway.  It���s also been advised there is a bridge farther down Sitze Road that may be compromised and is being assessed.  At this time, residence past this washout are un accessible.  Additional patrols of the area also discovered North Sushana Drive is impassible due to the Little Susitna River flooding the road.  These neighborhoods are also un accessible at this time. There were pictured posted on social media from the Alaska State Department of Transportation. SEOC also forwarded maps & pics of flooding in Houston. A news article with pictures can be seen here: https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/mat-su/2022/08/09/mat-su-flooding-closes-roads-threatens-homes-after-deluge-soaks-talkeetna-mountains/.

Numerous roads were closed in the Houston, AK township and up to 20 properties were affected. Flooding in the town of Houston and surrounding roads was widespread.   https://www.adn.com/alaska-news/mat-su/2022/08/09/mat-su-flooding-closes-roads-threatens-homes-after-deluge-soaks-talkeetna-mountains/  Flooding on the Little Susitna River at Houston reached a crest of 12.52 ft on August 10, 2022 at 5PM AKDT which was moderate flood stage.

The landspout tornado damaged some out buildings and ripped half the roof off an older mobile home which was one of the main damage indicators for this event. Several empty semi tractor trailers at a trucking company were flipped and pushed several yards. Toward the end of the damage path, the tornado destroyed a poorly constructed and old cabin/storage building. Power lines along the path were not damaged and a mobile home directly adjacent to the poorly constructed destroyed building only showed very minor damage. These factors suggest a high end EF0 rating with maximum winds around 85 mph. This survey utilized pictures and information provided by Moore County Emergency management. The landspout was well documented on video by numerous witnesses.
